raw: {"source": "def investigate(context, acquire):\n    return {\"query\": {\"actions\": [{\"op\": \"put\", \"id\": 5}, {\"op\": \"begin\"}, {\"op\": \"put\", \"id\": 9}, {\"op\": \"rollback\"}, {\"op\": \"put\", \"id\": 7}]}, \"note\": {\"obligation\": \"Return the AUTOINCREMENT id allocated after the actions.\", \"suspected\": \"Parent tracks only max ever inserted and ignores that rollback restores sqlite_sequence, so a later smaller put can lower the next id.\", \"evidence\": \"After rollback of put 9, table is {5}; put 7 makes max 7, so parent says 10 while SQLite AUTOINCREMENT should allocate 8.\", \"change\": \"Track the largest successfully committed/persisted inserted id and restore it on rollback; next id is that value plus 1.\"}}", "scope": "Rollback restores AUTOINCREMENT state, then a smaller explicit insert determines the next allocated id.", "change": "Replace max-ever tracking with persisted-high tracking that rollback restores; next id equals restored high plus 1."}
